title: Lot
lead: Abraham's nephew, who chose the well-watered plain near Sodom, was rescued from its destruction, and became the father of Moab and Ammon. The New Testament calls him "righteous Lot" (2 Peter 2:7), and Jesus warns, "Remember Lot's wife" (Luke 17:32).

sections.b: Israel is told not to attack Moab and Ammon, because God gave their land to "the sons of Lot" (Deuteronomy 2:9, 19; Psalm 83:8). Ruth the Moabite, a descendant of Lot's line, becomes David's great-grandmother (Ruth 4:13–22). Jesus compares his coming to the days of Lot and warns, "Remember Lot's wife" (Luke 17:28–32). 2 Peter 2:6–9 calls Lot righteous and distressed by the lawless, a picture of God rescuing the faithful.
sections.refs: Deuteronomy 2:9; Deuteronomy 2:19; Psalms 83:8; Ruth 4:13–22; Luke 17:28–32; 2 Peter 2:6–9
